campaigns.name: The Elemental Resistance to the Black Empire
campaigns.summary: A descriptive campaign grouping for the Elemental Lords' united attempt to remove the Old Gods and their growing empire.

campaigns.name: The Elemental Wars
campaigns.summary: A descriptive campaign grouping for the prolonged struggle among Azeroth's four elemental hosts.

campaigns.name: The Titan-forged War for Azeroth
campaigns.summary: An editorial campaign grouping for the keeper-led war that broke the Black Empire and made containment and planetary repair possible.

eras.name: The Age of Adventurers
eras.dateLabel: Research boundary — dates pending citation review
eras.summary: The period beginning with World of Warcraft: renewed faction conflict, Ahn'Qiraj, campaigns in Outland and Northrend, the Cataclysm, Pandaria, alternate Draenor, and the Legion's final invasion.

eras.name: Rise of the Ancient Civilizations
eras.dateLabel: Research boundary — dates pending citation review
eras.summary: The trolls and their empires, the aqir wars, the mogu, Pandaria, ancient humans, and the ascent of the kaldorei.

eras.name: Primordial Azeroth and the Black Empire
eras.summary: Azeroth's immense nascent world-soul left its native elementals without enough Spirit to balance them. Their long conflict was overtaken by the arrival of the Old Gods and the civilization their servants raised across the primordial world.

eras.name: Cosmic Origins
eras.dateLabel: Before the ordering of worlds · chronology without measured dates
eras.summary: Chronicle's account begins with Light and Shadow, the birth of the physical universe and Twisting Nether, the awakening of world-souls, the gathering of the titan Pantheon, and the Void Lords' attempt to corrupt a nascent titan through the Old Gods.

eras.name: The Long Vigil and the New Kingdoms
eras.dateLabel: Research boundary — dates pending citation review
eras.summary: The night elves guard Kalimdor while Quel'Thalas, Arathor, the Seven Human Kingdoms, Khaz Modan, and other post-Sundering powers develop.

eras.name: The Modern Cosmic Age
eras.dateLabel: Research boundary — dates pending citation review
eras.summary: The Fourth War, N'Zoth's return, Shadowlands, the awakening of the Dragon Isles, and Azeroth's increasingly direct role in the Worldsoul Saga.

eras.name: Ordering of Azeroth
eras.dateLabel: After the Black Empire · before the rise of ancient civilizations
eras.summary: The Pantheon intervenes to save Azeroth, the keeper-led titan-forged break the Black Empire, the surviving Old Gods are imprisoned, and the wounded world is stabilized and reshaped.

eras.name: The Rise of the Horde and the First Two Wars
eras.dateLabel: Research boundary — dates pending citation review
eras.summary: Draenor's corruption, the orcs' fall to the Legion, opening of the Dark Portal, destruction of Stormwind, and the Alliance victory in the Second War.

eras.name: The Third War and the Frozen Throne
eras.dateLabel: Research boundary — dates pending citation review
eras.summary: The Scourge, Arthas's downfall, destruction of Lordaeron and Quel'Thalas, the Legion's return, the Battle of Mount Hyjal, and the creation of the Lich King's new order.

eras.name: The War of the Ancients and the Sundering
eras.dateLabel: Research boundary — dates pending citation review
eras.summary: Queen Azshara, the Burning Legion's first invasion, the destruction of the Well of Eternity, and the shattering of primordial Kalimdor.

entities.name: Aggramar
entities.shortDescription: The titan who discovered the imperiled world of Azeroth and urged the Pantheon to act through purpose-built servants rather than overwhelming force.
entities.body: Aggramar recognized both the promise of Azeroth's sleeping world-soul and the danger posed by the Black Empire. Blizzard's first-party account emphasizes his concern that the Pantheon's colossal intervention could destroy what they meant to save.

entities.name: Al'Akir
entities.shortDescription: The cunning Elemental Lord of air, whose forces relied on spying, division, and sudden storms.

entities.name: Aman’Thul
entities.shortDescription: The first titan to awaken in Chronicle's account, who crossed the Great Dark in search of others of his kind.
entities.body: Aman’Thul's search gathered the awakened titans into the Pantheon. When the Pantheon confronted the corruption on Azeroth, his direct removal of Y'Shaarj revealed how deeply the Old Gods had rooted themselves in the world.

entities.name: Aqir
entities.shortDescription: Resilient insectoid servants formed from the Old Gods' organic matter and set to building the empire's cities and temples.

entities.name: Azeroth's World-Soul
entities.shortDescription: A titan spirit developing within the young world's core, whose immense growth drew in much of Azeroth's Spirit.
entities.body: Chronicle presents the world-soul as the reason Azeroth's elementals lacked the balancing fifth element. This record describes the primordial account and does not resolve later perspectives on Azeroth's nature.

entities.name: The Black Empire
entities.shortDescription: The civilization of Old God domains, citadels, and temple cities that spread across primordial Azeroth.
entities.body: The shaded atlas extent communicates broad influence only. Chronicle supports world-spanning expansion but does not provide survey-grade borders, so every boundary shown here is explicitly inferred.

entities.name: The Cosmic Forces
entities.shortDescription: Chronicle's cosmology arranges reality through opposed forces: Light and Shadow, Life and Death, and Order and Disorder.
entities.body: The familiar cosmology chart is used as a subject index, not copied as artwork. Later accounts may qualify how complete or objective this arrangement is.

entities.name: The Elemental Hosts
entities.shortDescription: The innumerable air, fire, earth, and water spirits led by Azeroth's four Elemental Lords.
entities.body: This collective editorial label groups the four rival elemental forces for battle playback. Chronicle describes them as separate hosts whose control of Azeroth shifted constantly, not as a permanent unified state.

entities.name: The Forge of Origination
entities.shortDescription: A southern titan-forged world-facility built to help stabilize Azeroth and retain a final re-origination safeguard against total corruption.
entities.body: The Forge worked in concert with the northern Forge of Wills. Its public overview states both its healing purpose and its terrible contingency without suggesting that the latter was used during this era.

entities.name: The Great Dark Beyond
entities.shortDescription: The physical universe of innumerable worlds and stars described in Chronicle's cosmological account.
entities.body: Its point on the cosmography is a reading aid only. A universe has not been reduced to a literal map marker.

entities.name: The Keepers
entities.shortDescription: The greatest titan-forged, empowered by members of the Pantheon to command the war and safeguard the ordering of Azeroth.
entities.body: The keepers led the armies that broke the Black Empire, contained the remaining Old Gods, stabilized the world-wound, established Ulduar, and directed the works that reshaped Azeroth. Individual duties are summarized here without turning the guided era into separate biographies.

entities.name: Light and Shadow
entities.shortDescription: Opposed primordial powers at the beginning of Chronicle's account of the Warcraft cosmos.
entities.body: This record keeps Chronicle Volume 1's creation account distinct from later cosmological perspectives. It does not claim that the diagram gives either power a physical location.

entities.name: Neptulon
entities.shortDescription: The Elemental Lord of water, portrayed as a patient strategist who struck divided rivals.

entities.name: N'raqi
entities.shortDescription: Intelligent servants formed from the Old Gods' organic matter and used as taskmasters within the expanding empire.

entities.name: The Old Gods
entities.shortDescription: Void-linked entities that struck Azeroth, spread corruption through the world, and drove tendrils toward its core.
entities.body: The Era 1 account treats the Old Gods collectively except where Chronicle specifically identifies Y'Shaarj. Later sources name and distinguish additional Old Gods; those records should be introduced only with their own citations.

entities.name: The Pantheon of Order
entities.shortDescription: A company of awakened titans who traveled the Great Dark, ordering worlds and seeking more world-souls.
entities.body: After discovering Azeroth's threatened world-soul, the Pantheon intervened against the Black Empire, empowered the keepers, and left the ordered world in their care.

entities.name: Primordial Kalimdor
entities.shortDescription: The largest continent of primordial Azeroth, shown here with an interpretive rather than surveyed outline.
entities.body: The source supports a single great continental setting and describes Y'Shaarj's civilization near its center. The exact coastline in this atlas is a reconstruction and must not be read as a measured canonical boundary.

entities.name: Ragnaros
entities.shortDescription: The Elemental Lord of fire, characterized by direct, destructive force against his rivals.

entities.name: Therazane
entities.shortDescription: The Elemental Lord of earth, protective of her children and defended by formidable mountain barriers.

entities.name: The Titan-forged
entities.shortDescription: Armies and workers of living stone and metal created to defeat the Black Empire, protect Azeroth, and help shape the wounded world.
entities.body: The first hosts fought beneath empowered keepers. Later titan-forged peoples undertook different labors across Azeroth, from raising mountains and tending machinery to carving waterways and guarding the keepers' works.

entities.name: The Twisting Nether
entities.shortDescription: A volatile astral realm formed from energies released around the creation of the physical universe.
entities.body: Chronicle describes the Nether as interwoven with the Great Dark Beyond while remaining distinct from it. The atlas uses no geographic distance between the two.

entities.name: Ulduar
entities.shortDescription: The keepers' great northern stronghold and the seat of the Forge of Wills during the ordering of Azeroth.
entities.body: Ulduar anchored the keepers' work in the far north of ancient Kalimdor. Its atlas marker is a broad reconstruction from that regional description, not a surveyed primordial coordinate.

entities.name: The Void Lords
entities.shortDescription: Shadow-aligned beings who sought to corrupt a world-soul but could not directly manifest their full power in the physical universe.
entities.body: Chronicle presents the Old Gods as instruments of this design. The record does not map the Void Lords to a physical territory.

entities.name: The Well of Eternity
entities.shortDescription: The immense arcane lake formed when the keepers stabilized the wound left by Y'Shaarj's removal.
entities.body: The Well was not created as an ornamental monument. It was Azeroth's exposed lifeblood brought into balance by wards, and its power would nourish life while shaping every era that followed.

entities.name: World-Souls
entities.shortDescription: Mysterious titan spirits that can form within some worlds and awaken after ages of growth.
entities.body: The record describes Chronicle Volume 1's titan account. It does not assert that every world contains such a soul.

entities.name: Y'Shaarj's Central Bastion
entities.shortDescription: An editorial label for the greatest Black Empire bastion, built around Y'Shaarj near the center of Azeroth's largest continent.
entities.body: Chronicle does not provide a proper name or exact coordinates for this bastion. The atlas marker is approximate and exists to communicate the source's near-the-center relationship, not a canonical point location.

entities.name: Y'Shaarj
entities.shortDescription: The Old God identified by Chronicle as the greatest of the group, surrounded by the Black Empire's largest bastion.

events.name: Awakening of Aman’Thul

date.label: After worlds formed within the Great Dark

events.summary: Aman’Thul awoke from the world that had nurtured his spirit and began searching the cosmos for other nascent titans.
events.description: The event name is an editorial label for the sequence described in Chronicle Volume 1.

events.name: Azeroth Is Ordered
events.summary: The titan-forged raised mountains, opened waterways, dredged seas, maintained great works, and helped make the wounded world stable enough for life to flourish.

events.name: Black Empire Dominion
events.summary: The elementals failed to dislodge the Old Gods and were enslaved; without that resistance, Black Empire influence extended over much of the world.

events.name: Rise of the Black Empire
events.summary: The n'raqi directed the aqir in building citadels and temple cities around the Old Gods; Y'Shaarj's central bastion became the greatest of these domains as their holdings spread.

events.name: Arrival of the Old Gods

date.label: After untold ages of elemental conflict

events.summary: A group of Old Gods struck Azeroth from the Great Dark, embedded themselves in different parts of the world, and extended their influence toward its core.

events.name: The Old Gods Are Contained

date.label: After the fall of the Black Empire

events.summary: Unable to remove the remaining Old Gods without repeating the wound caused by Y'Shaarj's destruction, the keepers bound them in prisons beneath Azeroth.

events.name: Scattering of the Old Gods

date.label: Before the Old Gods struck Azeroth

events.summary: The Void Lords made the Old Gods and cast them through the Great Dark, hoping that some would find and corrupt a world-soul.
events.description: The event name is an editorial label. The cosmography asserts sequence and purpose but no origin coordinate, route, or measurable number of Old Gods.

events.name: The Pantheon Departs
events.summary: With Azeroth stabilized and its guardians appointed, the Pantheon departed while the keepers and titan-forged remained to watch over the world.

events.name: The Pantheon Discovers Azeroth
events.summary: Aggramar discovered Azeroth's nascent titan and the Old Gods rooted around it, bringing the imperiled world to the Pantheon's attention.

events.name: Gathering of the Pantheon

date.label: During Aman’Thul's search for other titans

events.summary: The awakened titans found one another, formed the Pantheon, and traveled onward to order worlds and seek more of their kind.
events.description: The event name is an editorial label for the Pantheon's formation in Chronicle Volume 1.

events.name: Emergence of the Physical Universe

date.label: At the beginning of Chronicle's cosmic account

events.summary: The conflict between primordial Light and Void gave rise to the physical universe, while released energies formed the Twisting Nether.
events.description: The event name is an editorial label for the creation sequence described in Chronicle Volume 1; it is not presented as a formally named Warcraft event.

events.name: The Primordial Imbalance

date.label: Before the arrival of the Old Gods

events.summary: As Azeroth's world-soul developed, it consumed much of the fifth element, Spirit, leaving the native elementals without its balancing influence.
events.description: This descriptive event record captures Chronicle's causal explanation for the violent state of primordial Azeroth's elementals.

events.name: The Titan-forged Are Mustered
events.summary: The Pantheon created armies of stone and metal and empowered the greatest among them as keepers to lead the war for Azeroth.

events.name: The World-wound Is Stabilized

date.label: After the surviving Old Gods were imprisoned

events.summary: The keepers raised wards around Azeroth's bleeding wound until its arcane energies settled into the Well of Eternity.

events.name: The World-forges Are Established
events.summary: The keepers established complementary facilities in the far north and south to stabilize Azeroth and sustain the work of ordering it.

events.name: The Removal of Y'Shaarj

date.label: At the beginning of the Pantheon's intervention

events.summary: Aman’Thul tore Y'Shaarj from Azeroth, destroying the Old God but opening a terrible wound in the sleeping world-soul.

battles.name: The Elemental Assault on the Black Empire

date.label: After the Black Empire began to spread

battles.summary: For the first time, Azeroth's rival elemental hosts united against the Old Gods and attacked the Black Empire's growing cities.
battles.description: This descriptive title groups a broad conflict rather than asserting one localized battle. Chronicle describes firestorms and stone barriers striking Black Empire cities but does not provide mappable routes.

objectives.summary: Remove the Old Gods and their growing civilization from Azeroth.
Preserve and expand the Old Gods' domains through n'raqi and aqir forces.

phases.title: Rivals unite
phases.summary: The four elemental powers recognized a common threat.
phases.narration: As the Black Empire widened its shadow, the ancient enemies understood at last that none could stand alone. For the first time, Azeroth's elemental powers gathered against one foe.

phases.title: Firestorms cross the empire
phases.summary: Air and fire combined against Black Empire cities.
phases.narration: Wind and flame went forth together. Al'Akir's tempests bore the wrath of Ragnaros across the dark dominion, and immense firestorms descended upon the empire's citadels.

phases.title: Stone closes around the cities
phases.summary: Therazane raised barriers against the empire's settlements.
phases.narration: Then Therazane laid her strength upon the field. Jagged walls rose at her bidding, hemming in the servants of the Old Gods and breaking against their temple cities.

phases.title: The servant hosts endure
phases.summary: The empire answered through the n'raqi and aqir.
phases.narration: Yet from the cities came the n'raqi and the innumerable aqir. Rank after rank endured the elemental fury, until even the joined hosts could not overcome them.

phases.title: The resistance fails
phases.summary: The Old Gods defeated and enslaved the Elemental Lords.
phases.narration: In the end the resistance was broken. The Old Gods bound the Elemental Lords, and with no native power left to bar its way, the Black Empire spread across much of the world.

outcome.summary: The elemental resistance failed; the Elemental Lords were enslaved and the Black Empire extended its dominion over much of Azeroth.

battles.geographicEditorNote: The conflict covered multiple unnamed sites. No exact marker or route is asserted.

battles.name: The Elemental Wars

date.label: Untold ages before the Old Gods' arrival

battles.summary: The four Elemental Lords and their hosts fought across primordial Azeroth for ages, with dominion shifting continually and no lasting victor.
battles.description: The title is a descriptive grouping for Chronicle's world-spanning elemental conflict. Because the source supplies no stable front or exact battlefield, the atlas records its geography as unknown.

objectives.summary: Each rival elemental host sought dominion and the remaking of the world in its own image.

phases.title: The winds divide
phases.summary: Al'Akir weakened rivals through spies, deception, and sudden storms.
phases.narration: From the high airs Al'Akir watched the wars below. Through spies and deception he divided his enemies, and his tempests fell only when rival strength had already been spent.

phases.title: Fire overwhelms
phases.summary: Ragnaros answered strategy with volcanic, direct destruction.
phases.narration: Ragnaros placed no faith in subtle designs. Before him volcanoes opened, fire crowned the land, and ash followed where his overwhelming host had passed.

phases.title: Earth endures
phases.summary: Therazane sheltered behind mountains and counterattacked exhausted enemies.
phases.narration: Therazane gathered her children behind the strength of mountains. There they endured the fury of their foes, and only when the assault was weary did the earth rise to answer.

phases.title: Water divides and conquers
phases.summary: Neptulon waited for rival armies to separate before crushing them.
phases.narration: Neptulon did not squander his waters against a gathered host. He waited until the armies of his foes were divided, then loosed the deep against them in their weakness.

outcome.summary: No permanent victor emerged; control shifted while the conflict continued for untold ages.

battles.geographicEditorNote: Chronicle describes a world-spanning conflict without exact battle sites or stable fronts, so no marker or route is drawn.

battles.name: The Titan-forged War against the Black Empire
battles.summary: Keeper-led armies of stone and metal fought across primordial Azeroth, defeated the Black Empire's forces, and subdued the powers that had ruled the world.
battles.description: This title groups a world-spanning campaign described across Chronicle's Ordering sequence. The sources do not establish a surveyable front or one battle coordinate, so the atlas provides phases without an invented route or marker.

objectives.summary: Break the Black Empire while preserving Azeroth's nascent world-soul.
Hold the Old Gods' dominion against the keeper-led invasion.

phases.title: The keepers lead the hosts
phases.summary: Empowered keepers direct the first titan-forged armies into the corrupted world.
phases.narration: The keepers went before the hosts of living stone and metal. They did not come to conquer a kingdom for themselves, but to reach the power buried beneath it without destroying the world they had been made to save.

phases.title: The elemental powers are subdued
phases.summary: The titan-forged overcome the elemental forces bound to the Old Gods.
phases.narration: Storm, flame, stone, and sea rose against the invaders under the Old Gods' dominion. One by one those ancient powers were overcome, and the keepers prepared realms apart from the waking world in which the elemental hosts could be confined.

phases.title: The citadels are broken
phases.summary: The keeper-led hosts dismantle the Black Empire's military dominion.
phases.narration: Across unnamed fronts, the Black Empire's fortresses and servant hosts yielded. The sources give no single road by which the victory came, only a widening collapse as the titan-forged pressed toward the Old Gods themselves.

phases.title: The surviving Old Gods are bound
phases.summary: The remaining Old Gods are defeated and contained rather than torn from the world.
phases.narration: The lesson of the world-wound could not be ignored. The surviving Old Gods were not pulled free. They were overcome, chained, and sealed beneath Azeroth, so that their roots might remain without tearing the sleeping titan apart.

phases.title: A wounded world remains
phases.summary: Victory ends the empire but leaves a planet requiring containment and repair.
phases.narration: The empire had fallen, yet victory was not wholeness. Prisons lay beneath the earth, a wound burned at the continent's heart, and the keepers turned from war toward the longer labor of making Azeroth stable again.

outcome.summary: The Black Empire's rule was broken; its elemental powers were confined, the surviving Old Gods were imprisoned, and the keepers could begin healing and ordering Azeroth.

battles.geographicEditorNote: Chronicle describes a world-spanning campaign but does not provide an exact battle site, front line, or campaign route. No marker is asserted.

citations.section: Introduction: Cosmology and The Cosmic Forces
citations.note: Supports the cosmic frame and the roles of Light, Shadow/Void, Life, Death, Order, Disorder, and the elements.

citations.section: The Void Lords and the Old Gods
citations.note: Supports Chronicle's account of the Void Lords' world-soul objective, their limited manifestation in the physical universe, and the creation and scattering of the Old Gods. Pagination requires human confirmation against the selected complete edition.

citations.section: The Well of Eternity and the World Forges
citations.note: Supports the Old Gods' imprisonment, the keepers' stabilization of Azeroth's wound into the Well of Eternity, and the complementary world-forge system. Pagination requires human review.
Supports the stone-and-metal titan-forged, the empowered keepers, and their campaign against the Black Empire and its elemental servants. Pagination requires human review.
Research index for Chronicle-backed details about the empire's expansion, the elementals' defeat and enslavement, and the map depicting Azeroth under Black Empire control.

claims.value: Aggramar discovered Azeroth and recognized a nascent titan threatened by the Black Empire.

storyGuides.title: The Rise of the Black Empire
storyGuides.description: A guided history of primordial Azeroth, its elemental wars, the Old Gods' arrival, and the rise of the Black Empire.

storyGuides.title: Before the First World Was Ordered
storyGuides.description: A continuous guided history from Chronicle's primordial cosmic powers through the birth of the universe, the awakening of the titans, and the design that sent the Old Gods toward worlds such as Azeroth.

storyGuides.title: The Wounding and Ordering of Azeroth
storyGuides.description: A continuous history of the Pantheon's discovery, the costly first intervention, the titan-forged war, the containment of the Old Gods, and the long work that transformed a conquered world into ancient Kalimdor.

storyNodes.title: Before the empire
storyNodes.narration: Before mountain or sea had received a name, Azeroth's tale had already begun amid powers vaster than the world. Chronicle sets Light against Shadow, Life against Death, and Order against Disorder, while fire, air, earth, water, Spirit, and Decay shaped the mortal realm.

storyNodes.title: The sleeping titan within
storyNodes.narration: Deep within the young world, unseen beneath stone and flame, a mighty titan spirit stirred. As it grew, it drew heavily upon Spirit, the fifth element; and without that gentle balance, the native powers of Azeroth became restless and untamed.

storyNodes.title: Four powers without balance
storyNodes.narration: Four great lords arose above the tumult: Al'Akir, master of air; Ragnaros, lord of fire; Therazane, mother of earth; and Neptulon, ruler of water. Each desired dominion, and each carried war according to the nature of their element.

storyNodes.title: An age of elemental war
storyNodes.narration: Age followed uncounted age beneath storm, flood, fire, and heaving stone. The elemental hosts broke one another's realms and raised them anew, yet no victory endured; strife itself became the rhythm of primordial Azeroth.

storyNodes.title: The Old Gods descend
storyNodes.narration: Then the long contest was broken by a terror from beyond the heavens. The Old Gods fell from the Great Dark and rooted themselves in Azeroth. Around them the land withered, while their deep-reaching tendrils sought the sleeping world-soul below.

storyNodes.title: The empire's builders
storyNodes.narration: From the corrupted substance of the Old Gods arose servants shaped for their dark labor. The cunning n'raqi became taskmasters, and beneath their command the enduring aqir raised vast citadels and temple cities around their terrible masters.

storyNodes.title: A bastion near the world's center
storyNodes.narration: Greatest among those strongholds stood the bastion raised about Y'Shaarj, near the heart of Azeroth's largest continent. Its light upon this map is only approximate: Chronicle names its place in relation to the continent, but grants neither exact measure nor a proper city name.

storyNodes.title: The Black Empire spreads
storyNodes.narration: From that dreadful heart, the holdings of Y'Shaarj and the domains of the other Old Gods spread until together they formed the Black Empire. The boundary now revealed is a broad reconstruction of influence, not a surveyed frontier preserved by the source.

storyNodes.title: Old rivals form one resistance
storyNodes.narration: At last the ancient rivals beheld an enemy that threatened them all. For the first time the Elemental Lords stood together: wind bore fire against the empire, and earth rose against its cities. Yet even their joined wrath could not win the age.

storyNodes.title: A world awaiting the Ordering
storyNodes.narration: The Elemental Lords were defeated and bound, and the shadow of the Black Empire crept across much of Azeroth. Thus the primordial age darkened toward its end, until the Pantheon perceived the peril and sent titan-forged armies to answer it.

storyNodes.title: Before time could be counted
storyNodes.narration: Before any world carried mountain, sea, or name, Chronicle begins with a boundless opposition. Light shone without measure, and beyond its reach gathered Shadow—the Void. They were not kingdoms upon a chart, but primordial powers, divided in nature and bound within the first telling of the cosmos.

storyNodes.title: The Great Dark opens
storyNodes.narration: Where Light and Void pressed against one another, their conflict broke the stillness. From that violence came the physical universe: the Great Dark Beyond, immense and cold, kindled with newborn stars. Here at last were distance and matter, though no mortal witness stood beneath those first and ancient fires.

storyNodes.title: A storm beside creation
storyNodes.narration: Yet creation did not settle into silence. Unstable energies gathered into the Twisting Nether, a volatile astral realm interwoven with the Great Dark and unlike its ordered substance. The nearness shown here is only the nearness of one thought to the next; no source grants these realms a measured border.

storyNodes.title: Powers that shape reality
storyNodes.narration: Across this vast account stand six great forces. Light answers Shadow; Life answers Death; Order answers Disorder. Fire, air, earth, water, Spirit, and Decay move within the mortal realm beneath them. This is Chronicle's framework, offered here as a lantern for the story—not as the last word on every mystery.

storyNodes.title: Dreamers in the deep
storyNodes.narration: Among the countless worlds, some bore a presence hidden far below their crust: a titan spirit, sleeping while ages passed above. Such world-souls grew slowly within their wandering homes. If one endured and awakened, it rose no longer as a world alone, but as a living titan of immeasurable power.

storyNodes.title: The first titan wakes
storyNodes.narration: First among them to wake was Aman’Thul. He looked into the lonely reaches of the Great Dark and understood that others of his kind might still dream within distant worlds. So the Highfather began his long search, crossing the newborn heavens and calling to the spirits he found sleeping there.

storyNodes.title: The Pantheon gathers
storyNodes.narration: One by one, awakened titans answered, until Aman’Thul no longer walked the cosmos alone. Together they became the Pantheon. Where they found worlds wounded or disordered, they labored to bring stability; and beyond each ordered horizon, they continued the search for brethren who had not yet opened their eyes.

storyNodes.title: A design cast into darkness
storyNodes.narration: The Void Lords also sought the sleeping titans, but could not pour their full strength into the physical universe. In their hunger they shaped the Old Gods and hurled them blindly through the Great Dark. Their hope was dreadful and patient: that one might strike a world-soul and corrupt it before awakening.

storyNodes.title: One world among the stars
storyNodes.narration: Across that immeasurable dark turned a young world called Azeroth, bearing within it a titan spirit of extraordinary might. The Old Gods would find this world before the Pantheon understood its peril. There the cosmic design narrowed into earth, flame, storm, and sea—and the long age of the Black Empire drew near.

storyNodes.title: The world the keepers inherited
storyNodes.narration: The tale begins where the Black Empire left the world: beneath a dominion of citadels, servant hosts, and powers rooted deeper than any mountain. Azeroth's sleeping spirit endured below them, mighty beyond measure and yet unable to cast the corruption from its own skin. Nothing upon the world remained strong enough to break that reign.

storyNodes.title: A watcher finds the hidden world
storyNodes.narration: Far beyond those clouded skies, Aggramar found Azeroth. He perceived the nascent titan within, and also the Old Gods fastening their will around it. The news passed to the Pantheon like a bell across the Great Dark. Here was a spirit of extraordinary promise; here too was a peril that could turn such promise against all creation.

storyNodes.title: Victory becomes a wound
storyNodes.narration: Aman’Thul reached toward the greatest of the Old Gods and tore Y'Shaarj from the world. The horror was destroyed, but its roots had entered too deeply. Stone, empire, and corruption came away together, and Azeroth's arcane lifeblood surged from the wound. In that instant the Pantheon learned that strength alone might kill the one it sought to save.

storyNodes.title: Hands of stone and metal
storyNodes.narration: The answer was not another titan's grasp. At Aggramar's urging, the Pantheon fashioned servants whose power could be brought against the Black Empire without shattering Azeroth beneath their feet. From stone and metal came the first titan-forged hosts: soldiers made for the war before them, and workers for labors not yet begun.

storyNodes.title: The keepers take command
storyNodes.narration: Among the titan-forged, the Pantheon raised a smaller company to bear greater power and judgment. These were the keepers. They would command the hosts, answer changing danger with more than brute force, and remain when distant makers had gone. Beneath their direction, the armies entered a world whose every horizon belonged to the enemy.

storyNodes.title: The long dominion breaks
storyNodes.narration: The war passed across fronts whose roads are no longer known. The titan-forged overcame the elemental powers bound to the Old Gods, broke servant hosts, and cast down the Black Empire's strongholds. No single stroke ended that shadow. It receded through a world-spanning campaign until the keepers stood before the powers beneath the empire itself.

storyNodes.title: Chains beneath the earth
storyNodes.narration: The surviving Old Gods could not be torn out without opening new wounds. Thus the keepers chose containment. The defeated horrors were bound in prisons beneath Azeroth, near enough to remain a danger, yet held from the sleeping titan's heart. Victory had not erased the corruption. It had made the long guarding of it possible.

storyNodes.title: The wound becomes a well
storyNodes.narration: At the continent's heart, Azeroth still bled light into the open world. The keepers labored around that ruin, raising wards until the torrent quieted and its power found balance. What remained was named the Well of Eternity: not a scar made beautiful, but a scar kept from becoming the death of the world.

storyNodes.title: Two forges hold the world
storyNodes.narration: The work spread from the Well toward two great engines. In the far north, Ulduar held the Forge of Wills. Far to the south stood the Forge of Origination, made both to strengthen the wounded world and, should corruption become absolute, to begin it anew. Between them passed the hidden labor of preservation.

storyNodes.title: Mountains rise, and rivers find the sea
storyNodes.narration: Then began the labor by which victory became a world. Titan-forged hands raised ranges, opened deep places, cut waterways, dredged seas, tended engines, and guarded what had been built. The keepers fostered places where living things could flourish. When they looked across the primary continent they had shaped, they called it Kalimdor, the land beneath eternal starlight.

storyNodes.title: The makers pass beyond the sky
storyNodes.narration: At last the Pantheon judged Azeroth guarded well enough to leave. The keepers remained beside their forges, prisons, and appointed works, while the titan-forged watched a quieter horizon. Yet the ordered world was no finished monument. Around the Well, life would change, gather memory, and raise powers of its own. The age of ancient civilizations waited beyond the dawn.
